_comment: THE DESK REGISTRY — one authoritative list of every declared desk.
This file is NOT a desk manifest and is deliberately not discoverable as
one. core.manifests.load_all_desks() globs desks/*/manifest.json; this
file sits one level up, so declaring a desk here cannot make
sync_desk_config() write a desk, institution or source row into the
tracked production database, and cannot enable collection.
What a desk's manifest says is authoritative for its SOURCES. What this
file says is authoritative for its STATUS and its public presentation.
Neither invents the other: configured and enabled source counts are read
from the manifest this file points at, and a desk with no manifest has no
sources — which is a fact, not a gap to fill in.
Record counts are never declared here. They come from the database, for
desks that have records in it.
Statuses (core/domain.py DESK_STATUSES):
planned        declared scope, nothing researched or configured
research       scope researched; no enabled source and nothing
collecting. A collector may be built and rehearsed,
but it has not been launched
shadow         collecting privately under evaluation; no public records
live           collecting into the production corpus
paused         configured and deliberately stopped
access_blocked researched and reachable in principle, but official
discovery is not available under honest identification

desks.name: China Desk
desks.scope: Chinese official and state-linked defense publication surfaces: the armed forces newspaper, the defense ministry, the state news agency's military desk, and two English-language portals.
desks.status_explanation: Collecting daily into the production corpus. This is the only mature collection in the project.
limits: Coverage is selective and heavily concentrated in one source.
Not every Chinese official publication surface is implemented. One configured source has no working collector and is reported as such on every run rather than hidden.
Collection was interrupted between 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-24. The gap is preserved, not backfilled.

desks.name: Singapore Desk
desks.scope: One publication family: official releases from the Singapore Ministry of Defence, which publishes for itself and for the Singapore Armed Forces.
desks.status_explanation: Promoted 2026-09-21 (DECISION_LOG), after 33 elapsed shadow-collection days, completed Day 7 and Day 14 human checkpoint reviews, and owner sign-off. The corpus began as a one-time governed promotion of 57 corrected shadow records; the same adapter, already run daily by the shadow collector since 2026-08-19, is now also invoked by the ordinary scheduled production pipeline, so the corpus grows from further scheduled runs going forward. Two records stay held out of the promotable set for unrepaired charset damage.
limits: This is not whole-of-government coverage, not armed-forces-wide, and not comprehensive Singapore defense coverage.
Other ministries, the parliamentary Hansard record, unit and recruitment pages, magazine features, social media, and procurement notices are all outside the declared scope.
The corpus began as a one-time governed promotion; new records are now collected by the ordinary scheduled production pipeline, subject to the same held-record exclusions.

Two records are held out of the promoted corpus: their CJK text was damaged by a historical extractor defect the correction overlay could not repair, and they are excluded rather than published with damaged text. See shadow/singapore_mindef/CORRECTIONS.md for which records and why.

qualification.explanation: Historical qualification record, retained after promotion rather than deleted: this is evidence for how the desk reached live status, not a current gate. Day zero was 2026-08-19T23:03:09Z. Day 7 and Day 14 human checkpoint reviews are complete, both pass_with_findings, published to review/singapore-mindef. No separate Day 30 human checkpoint review is on record; the review kit's computed Day-30 packet reproduces byte-for-byte and reports publishable: yes. Owner sign-off promoting the desk to live is recorded in DECISION_LOG.md, 2026-09-21.

desks.name: Japan Desk
desks.scope: Official Japanese-language Ministry of Defense RSS discovery from its news and site-update streams, plus a separate Japan Coast Guard English press-release shadow pilot. Neither covers all Japanese defense or maritime-security publications, and neither MOD feed represents Joint Staff or English MOD releases.
desks.status_explanation: Japan remains shadow-only. The two MOD Japanese-language RSS feeds support official discovery, but body retrieval is partial: some PDF-published originals yield extractable text while most HTML articles are challenged and retained only as dated discovery metadata. Separately, a Japan Coast Guard English HTML pilot has one verified, manually authorized October 8 Day 0. The guarded daily gate was observed unset or unavailable in an October 12 read-only Actions run, so no subsequent JCG collecting-day continuity is established; linked PDF/media rights remain held. Nothing from either source family is admitted to the production corpus, and neither proves complete Japanese defense or maritime-security coverage.

research.volume_caveat: These figures describe what the ministry published and what its feeds carry. They are not a record count and nothing here has been collected into the public record. Only PDF-format originals have yielded usable MOD text in the current shadow archive; on the news feed that was 8 of 142 items in the 2026-08-26 baseline. The October 11 ledger preserves just five text-bearing originals and 158 unretrieved URLs; extracted text is not certified as the complete PDF including imagery.
blockers: Documents published as HTML cannot be retrieved.

The ministry's RSS feeds and some PDF documents are served, but other PDFs fail fetch or extraction checks and HTML documents on the same host are returned behind an interactive challenge. Those items are discovered and recorded as unretrieved rather than inferred to be absent. An institution that wants to refuse this collector must be able to recognise it and say so, so defeating the challenge would destroy the capability that rule protects. Resolving this means requesting an official route.
MOD PDF source completeness and qualification remain unresolved.

The 30 verified scheduled MOD collection slots from September 12 through October 11 all reported partial source health: five archived text-bearing originals, 158 unresolved retrieval gaps at the latest ledger, and no complete document-level PDF fidelity or signed Day 7/14/30 source approvals. Do not interpret scheduled operation as publisher completeness or production qualification.
resolved: The listing pages remain challenged, but the ministry publishes two official RSS feeds that are served normally and support conditional requests. Discovery no longer depends on the challenged pages.
PDF text extraction wired to a collector — resolved 2026-08-26.
The dormant extractor is now used by the Japan shadow adapter, and by nothing on the production collection path.

On the 2026 listing “Japan-U.S. Bilateral Exercise” appears 27 times for distinct events, and a title-only rule would collapse 26 of those 27 records. Deduplication is by canonical URL and by content hash of the extracted text, never by title, so a recurring ministry title stays as many records as there were publications.

limits: No source is enabled in production. Nothing collected here reaches the production database, the public site, or any public count.

Retrieval is partial. On 2026-08-26, 8 of 142 news-feed items (6 percent) were PDF-format candidates and 134 were HTML; the PDF count did not establish usable or complete full text, while challenged HTML bodies were recorded as unretrieved metadata. This is not complete Ministry of Defense or Joint Staff coverage.

The MOD feeds are Japanese-language. The Ministry's English press releases and Joint Staff remain access-challenged and uncollected. The separate JCG English pilot has a specifically approved manual source observation dated October 8, 2026; its repository gate was observed unset or unavailable on October 12 and no daily continuity, production admission or per-document rights clearance is established.

MOD RSS shadow testing began 2026-08-26, and 30 scheduled MOD collection slots from September 12 to October 11 were independently verified but all partial; named Day 7/14/30 human source reviews remain unsigned. JCG's separate manual Day 0 was 2026-10-08 with no verified daily continuity. These distinct collection clocks confer no source publication authority.

desks.name: South Korea Desk
desks.scope: Source-verified Ministry of National Defense (국방부) official-link metadata, separately licensed Korean government original text, and editor-approved English translation and analysis. The historical bibliography is selective, and DAPA collection remains research-only pending independently verified article identities and rights.
desks.status_explanation: MND link-only metadata has been admitted to a separately controlled production table, and licensed source-text and approved bilingual/editorial pages are published through distinct guarded workflows. The full-country desk retains a shadow registry status: DAPA and comprehensive Korean defense coverage have not been promoted.

source_families.note: Publisher 대한민국 정책브리핑, distinct original issuer 방위사업청 (B00008). Separately, the DAPA-operated dapa.go.kr press list passed a robots-first read-only listing observation, but its dated interactive rows lack verified row-to-article identities. The October 8 portal samples include HWPX and PDF variants of the same releases. DAPA article/attachment capture, item-local issuer and content-rights qualification, daily collection and production admission remain unapproved.

research.volume_caveat: Five original bibliography entries come from immutable October 11 source evidence; nine further official-link references remain separately frozen. Independently qualified future MND link metadata and KOGL-scoped Korean originals may be added under separate production release policies. Neither these lanes nor the selectively approved English analyses establish comprehensive Ministry or DAPA coverage.
blockers: Broader Korean source interpretation and coverage remain incomplete.

Three specifically reviewed English translations and source-grounded analytical releases are publicly registered, but no machine-only assessment can be represented as independently verified research. Future drafts require editor approval, and DAPA-specific article evidence is not qualified.
Original files, third-party media and unreviewed sources remain excluded.

Separately approved KOGL Type 1 Korean source text may be reproduced with attribution. That scope does not clear the HWPX file itself, photographs, graphics, videos, third-party works, or any later unreviewed source; such material is not mirrored.
Production collector promotion is separate.

An operational MND metadata feed and item-specific source-text/English approvals do not promote the entire country desk or DAPA feed, assert countrywide completeness, or confer model-generated editorial authority. Sustained reliability and separate DAPA verification remain required.
resolved: Private SHA-pinned reader and real-source verification operate.

Those October 11 private verification stages were followed by production MND metadata admission, owner-approved Korean-text publication and exact public HTTPS readback. Three original-text source identities and their three separately reviewed English/analysis pairs are in current approved release registries. Publisher evidence, rights and editorial status are source-specific.

Five fixed MND bibliography entries and nine additional official links remain distinguishable from separately admitted live MND metadata and licensed original-text/editorial publication. None of these references alone independently corroborates a government factual claim.

limits: Five original plus nine additional bibliographic links are not counted as independently archived originals. Separately governed production MND link metadata, licensed text and reviewed English are explicitly listed elsewhere; their existence does not establish comprehensive Korean defense coverage.

The admitted MND source family identifies 국방부 as issuer and Korea Policy Briefing as republisher; it is not direct MND.gov.kr collection. DAPA is a separate unadmitted issuer with a read-only first-party listing observation and a different prospective source-access and rights decision.

Bibliography records retain links and dates; separately qualified Korean original-text pages and independently approved English translations/analyses are public. HWPX, PDF binaries, photographs, diagrams and videos are not mirrored merely because article text qualifies for reuse.

Official source claims remain attributed, not independently verified facts. Portal posting and ministry distribution dates remain distinct. No DAPA production or automatic source-to-editorial approval is authorized.

AFP has preserved originals under review; the NSC source had no articles at the pinned October 11 snapshot. Neither is admitted to the production IPR corpus, and reliability, human source-review and rights gates remain incomplete.

Publisher-specific rights and canonical evidence custody remain unresolved.

research.observed_volume_subject: Items the defense tag page listed
research.volume_caveat: Counted from the tag page as it was read on 2026-10-06 UTC. These figures count what editors tagged, not the newsroom's defense output, and the page reaches back only 24 items, so 2023 is cut short. They are not a record count, and nothing has been collected into the public record. At the rate listed, most days will list nothing new, and a day with nothing new shows only that the listing was read, not that article text can be retrieved.
blockers: Government News remote dispatch remains unapproved.

The Government News English defense-tag collector has no approved remote dispatch and is separate from the operating Vietnamese MPS and MOIT ministry shadow families. Its pilot does not establish production readiness.
A tag is not a category.

The tag lists what Government News editors chose to tag. When it was read, the national security strategy summary of 4 August 2026 carried no tag at all, and a Politics item of 23 September 2026 on a meeting with the acting U.S. Navy Secretary was not on the tag page. Items the tag does not list are not collected and nothing is claimed about them; no keyword or topic filter is used to fill the gap.
The tag page shows only its 24 most recent items.

Older items load by script from an address the page never publishes as a link, and that address is not requested. An item that appears on the page after its date's window was read is reported by the review rather than silently absorbed. No archive completeness is claimed.
The ministry and the army newspaper were not reachable.

The ministry's robots.txt returned a script page instead of a policy, and the newspaper's listings redirected to themselves. Both are recorded as measured and left alone: an institution must be able to recognise this collector and refuse it. Reading either would need an official route.
Collection-health thresholds remain unset.

Publication cadence and silence thresholds are calibrated only after shadow collection has run. On a tag this sparse a long quiet stretch is ordinary, so guessing now would create false alarms or hide real silence.

limits: No source is enabled in production for Vietnam, and no shadow record contributes to public counts. MPS/MOIT ministry sources run on separate isolated daily shadow cadence; National Defence Journal has no active collection, remote dispatch, state or reliability clock.

Bounded newsroom and ministry publication families only. No comprehensive Vietnamese defense coverage, no complete ministry archive, no People’s Army Newspaper collection and no formal-document family.
Government News is the Government's newsroom. Its reports are not ministry statements, and a report that names a resolution or quotes a minister remains a newsroom report about it.
English and Vietnamese as published, in separate source families. No translation or recovered-original claim.

The three ministry families established remote Day 0 on 2026-10-07; required 7/14/30 human reviews and source-level rights gates remain. National Defence Journal is research-only and cannot inherit those ministry clocks or count as qualified.

desks.name: Indonesia Desk
desks.scope: A bounded institutional-news research desk focused initially on Kementerian Pertahanan Republik Indonesia (Kemhan) Berita, in original Indonesian. Coverage excludes the armed forces' wider publications, ministerial decrees, and national defense-policy documents.
desks.status_explanation: Kemhan Berita is collected on a separate scheduled shadow-state branch for private source evaluation. Its original Indonesian articles are not in the public IPR corpus. Fifteen dated Berita links and two historical Siaran Pers press links provide attributed outbound navigation only; neither group constitutes human-reviewed IPR citations or public archive records. Five preserved originals received preliminary review; independent Indonesian-language signoff and the Day 7/14/30 collection reviews remain outstanding.

source_families.name: Indonesian Ministry of Defense — Berita (Indonesian)
source_families.format: Dated ministry news HTML; isolated shadow preservation and private research reader
source_families.note: Institutional Berita statements on www.kemhan.go.id, not verbatim official decrees, treaties or independent verification of military capability. Original-language article text stays in shadow state. No publisher bodies, photographs or translations are displayed here.

source_families.name: Indonesian Ministry of Defense — Siaran Pers (Indonesian)
source_families.format: Disabled parser candidate; no authorized collection
source_families.note: Separate sparse press-release family; two 2026 ministry press statements have metadata-only outbound links, but the parser remains disabled and there is no press collector or preserved Siaran Pers state. Berita collection continuity does not establish press reliability or reuse rights.

blockers: Original-language editorial review

Private captured Berita originals have undergone assistant-assisted integrity and focused factual checks, not named Indonesian-language editorial certification. A publisher geographic inconsistency on one article and other factual qualifications require independent review before reviewed citations, translated analysis or corpus admission.
Source-specific publisher rights

The Kemhan site identifies ministry copyright; IPR has no documented blanket licence to republish its articles, images or translations. Both public-link groups point outward to seventeen first-party pages (fifteen Berita and two Siaran Pers); neither permits republication of publisher originals, photographs or translations.
Collection reliability and eligibility
The initial isolated collection began October 6, 2026. The October 11 evidence preflight cannot satisfy the October 13 Day 7 checkpoint, later human Day 14/30 reviews or 30-day corpus-admission test.
Scope is not nationwide coverage

Kemhan institutional news alone cannot establish complete coverage of Indonesian defense, individual services, parliament, or formal policy documents. Siaran Pers and other agencies remain separate disabled or unreviewed sources.

limits: Fifteen Berita and two Siaran Pers first-party links are available for navigation; no article body, model analysis or independently reviewed citation is published, and Indonesia has no admitted public corpus records.
Isolated shadow collection is not production collection. A daily collection-success ledger does not establish completeness of ministry releases.
Original Berita reports represent the ministry's communication, not independent confirmation of outcomes, agreements, force readiness or project completion.
Named Indonesian-language, content-rights and Day 7/14/30 decisions still govern reviewed citation releases and production admission; outbound official links are not article-republication approval.

desks.name: US Indo-Pacific Reference Desk
desks.scope: Declared as a reference desk, deliberately bounded: the minimum US institutional output needed to read other desks' framing against a US framing of the same events. It is not a feed of US defense releases.
desks.status_explanation: Declared scope only, and access-blocked at the edge. Probed once per endpoint on 2026-08-26 with the project user agent: the site root, the Press Releases and Readouts listing, and robots.txt itself all return HTTP 403 from the edge. An RSS endpoint does answer, but robots.txt cannot be read, so there is no basis on which to say collection is permitted. Collecting only through the one endpoint that happens to answer, while the same edge refuses everything else including the file that would state the rules, would be opportunistic rather than honest.
limits: Nothing has been configured, enabled or collected.
robots.txt returns 403, so this project cannot establish that collection is permitted. That is a blocker on its own, independent of whether any endpoint answers.

The institution's current name is U.S. Pacific Command, restored in 2026. If a source is ever built, its identity follows the institution's own name even though the desk stays geographically labeled Indo-Pacific.

If it is ever built it is collected under the same contract, health thresholds and evidence hierarchy as every other desk. U.S. institutional statements are evaluated under the same source-verification and editorial standards as every other desk; they are not treated as independent confirmation of their own claims.
